event_chain.action: Atum-Kheprer arises upon primeval hill as the ben-bird of Heliopolis
Atum spits out Shu and sputters out Tefnut
Atum embraces Shu and Tefnut with ka arms, investing them with his divine ka
Speaker petitions Atum to encircle and guard King Nefer-ka-Re and his pyramid for eternity
Atum begets the Great Ennead of Heliopolis with joy in his heart
Speaker invokes the Ennead never to separate from Atum as he protects the king and pyramid

id: Egyptian myth #2 (Contest of Horus and Seth)

event_chain.action: Horus and Seth dispute succession to Osiris's throne before the divine tribunal
The tribunal writes to goddess Neith requesting arbitration on the eighty-year inheritance case
Neith decrees that Osiris's office be awarded to Horus and Seth given compensation
Re-Har-akhti rejects the verdict, asserting Horus is too young and weak to rule
Seth threatens violence against the gods over Isis's intervention, isolating the court on Central Island
Isis disguises herself, crosses to the island, and tricks Seth into validating Horus's rightful claim
Seth challenges Horus to an underwater endurance ordeal disguised as hippopotamuses
Horus decapitates Isis after she spares Seth, and Seth blinds Horus before Hathor heals his eyes
Seth challenges Horus to a stone-ship race; Horus floats a plastered wooden craft while Seth's stone ship sinks
Thoth writes to Osiris requesting a binding judgment on the claimants
Osiris threatens to loose ferocious underworld messengers if justice is denied to Horus
Tribunal brings bound Seth in defeat and crowns Horus king of Egypt with the White Crown
Re-Har-akhti takes Seth to live as a son beside him in heaven to thunder from the sky
Worshippers offer formal praise and adoration to Aten rising on the eastern horizon
Aten sets in the west, casting the earth into deathlike darkness, stillness, and prowling predators
Aten rises at dawn, banishing shadows and awakening mankind, herds, and flora to life and labor
Aten generates life within woman, infuses breath into the fetus, and nurtures infants and chicks
Aten creates the diverse nations, varied tongues, and skin colors while dwelling alone
Aten creates the underworld Nile for Egypt and places a celestial Nile of rain in heaven for foreign nations
Aten institutes changing seasons of winter coolness and summer heat to rear all living things
Aten reveals divine mysteries and plans solely to his royal son Akhenaten and Queen Nefertiti
Amon-Re welcomes and embraces Thutmose III, bestowing valor and worldwide dominion upon him
Amon-Re binds vast multitudes of Nubian and northern enemies as living captives under the pharaoh's feet
Amon-Re leads the pharaoh past the Euphrates bend and sets the royal uraeus to devour rebellious foes
Thutmose III manifests as solar radiance, falling star, and bull to crush chiefs of Djahi and Retenu
Pharaoh courses like a jackal of the south, trampling front lands and binding Sand-Dwellers as captives
Pharaoh tramples Nubian barbarians as far as Shat-Djeba, protected by divine brothers and sisters
Amon-Re confirms Thutmose III on the throne of Horus for eternity in return for magnificent temple monuments
Righteous man rejects counsel of ungodly, path of sinners, and assembly of scorners
Righteous person delights in and meditates upon the law of the Lord day and night
Righteous person flourishes and prospers like a fruitful tree planted by streams of water
The ungodly are scattered and driven away by wind like weightless chaff
Ungodly and sinners fail to stand in divine judgment or enter congregation of the righteous
The Lord upholds the way of the righteous while the path of the wicked perishes
Heathen nations and kings conspire and rebel against the Lord and his anointed king
Rebellious rulers resolve to break divine bonds and throw off their cords
The Lord derides the rebels from heaven and speaks to them in terrifying wrath
The Lord establishes his king upon holy hill Zion, proclaiming him his begotten Son
The Lord promises the nations and ends of the earth as an inheritance to the Son
The king is empowered to break rebels with an iron rod and dash them like clay pottery
Earthly kings are commanded to submit to the Son and revere the Lord to avert ruin
Raven-Man and Little-Bird-Man compete to woo Big-Raven's daughter
Raven-Man eats carrion in secret while pretending to be an expert hunter
Big-Raven promises his daughter to whichever suitor calms a prolonged blizzard
Raven-Man urinates in his boots under a cliff and gives up, claiming the sky is broken
Little-Bird-Man flies to the cleft in heaven, plugs it with a stopper and fat, calming the storm
Big-Raven banishes filthy Raven-Man and gives daughter Yinia-nawgut to Little-Bird-Man
Vengeful Raven-Man hides the sun in his mouth like a quid, plunging the land into darkness
A daughter sings while groping for water in the dark; River-Man assists and marries her
Yinia-nawgut visits Raven-Man, tickles him until he laughs, releasing the trapped sun into heaven
Yinia-nawgut flatters Raven-Man, brings him home, and kills him, mounting his palate to ensure clear skies
Little-Bird-Man insists on carrying his wife across a swollen river on foot and dies
Little-Bird-Man reappears as a wealthy reindeer herder, proves his identity with mittens, and returns home in joy
Big-Raven scatters dancing mouse-girls into water and mud, seizing their stranded baby seal
Mice drop magical enchanted grass into Big-Raven's house so he postpones eating the cooked seal until morning
Mice steal the seal meat and broth while ravens sleep, defecating in the kettle and loading boots with pebbles
Big-Raven encounters stones in boots and foul broth, taking up a club to attack the mouse-women
Mice soothe angry Big-Raven with cloudberry pudding and fasten red cloth shreds to his eyelids as he naps
Big-Raven mistaking red rags for fire orders his wife to tear their son in half before realizing the trick
Big-Raven returns with his club; mice ply him with berry pudding and blacken his face with charcoal during sleep
Mice send Big-Raven to river where he sees his painted reflection, courts it as Painted-Woman, and drowns himself
Tribe refuses hungry Wurrunnah food seeds, driving him to depart in anger for strange lands
Wurrunnah encounters eyeless honey hunter, vanishing lagoon, terrifying bark spirit, and mistakenly spears featherless man
Wurrunnah reaches encampment of seven Meamei sisters who shelter and feed him
Wurrunnah trails sisters to ant mounds and steals two digging sticks while they feast
Wurrunnah sticks stolen implements into earth and ambushes two searching sisters, capturing them as wives
Wurrunnah compels captive wives to cut pine bark despite warnings of perpetual loss
Pine trees shoot upward into the sky carrying both sisters on their expanding trunks
Five sisters in heaven pull the two rising sisters into the sky to abide together forever as the Pleiades
Iguana father and mother bird abandon young Cookooburrah brothers without water in camp
Eldest brother finds perishing brothers, scales water-tree goolahgool, and splits trunk to release torrent
Young brothers quench thirst and bathe rejoicing in the swelling stream
Eldest brother directs siblings to deceive returning parents into wading across the dangerous deep current
Children mock drowning mother's pleas for a branch with laughing cries from the safety of the riverbank
Rushing flood sweeps away and drowns neglectful parents in retribution
Deity creates first Amis ancestor Masera in ancestral land Arapanay
Ancestor Masera fathers two sons Tapang Masera and Rarog Masera
Spirits generate ocean current carrying brothers to Chippong river mouth in Taitung
Brothers designate landing place Arapanay in memory of original homeland
A god plants a wooden staff in the earth
The planted staff metamorphoses into a living bamboo plant
Bamboo sprouts two shoots that transform into male and female first ancestors
Offspring of primeval ancestors multiply and occupy Kouasain near Puyuma
